name: research-lab
description: Ask one question and walk away. Research Lab turns it into a tree of sub-questions and works that tree down over many unattended cycles: each hourly cycle hands a few open sub-questions to their own subagents, records what came back with its sources, and grafts on whatever new questions the work raised. When the tree is answered — or the cycle budget runs out — it synthesises everything into one markdown report on your machine.
author: PersonalClaw

crons.name: advance-campaigns
crons.message:
Advance the open Research Lab campaign by one cycle.

1. Call research_next. If its metadata says done: true, call research_report once and stop — do not open a new campaign.
2. Otherwise take the worklist it returns and research each sub-question in its own subagent, in parallel, so one slow question does not stall the cycle.
3. For each answered sub-question call research_record with the finding, the sources it rests on, and any follow-up questions the work raised.
4. Stop after this one cycle. The next cron tick runs the next one.

Record what you actually found, including "no reliable source says" — an unattended campaign is only worth reading if its findings are honest.

x-meta.label: Default cycle budget
x-meta.help: How many unattended cycles a new campaign may run before it stops and asks to be synthesised. A research_open call can override it per campaign.

x-meta.label: Sub-questions per cycle
x-meta.help: How many sub-questions one cycle hands out to subagents. A research_next call can override it per cycle.
